The Next Million,

Every Engine of Growth in Motion
Crossing the two-million annual sales milestone marked an important chapter in the Company's growth journey. At that 
stage, the pathway to the next million appeared longer as the passenger vehicle industry grappled with affordability 
challenges, which constrained participation from first-time buyers and slowed the natural expansion of the market. 
FY 2025-26 marked an important turning point in that context.
The revival of the small car segment, supported by GST reduction, reactivated an important growth engine for the 
industry. At the same time, the Company strengthened its SUV portfolio, sustained export growth and expanded its 
multi-powertrain creating, fresh momentum in its growth trajectory. What makes this phase particularly significant is that 
growth is no longer dependent on a single driver. Multiple engines of growth are now moving simultaneously, making 
the journey to the next million sales milestone appear faster than previously anticipated. Reflecting this confidence, the 
Company is accelerating its capacity expansion plans and has added 500,000 units of manufacturing capacity during 
FY 2026-27.
Looking ahead, the Company plans to introduce seven SUVs over the next five years, reinforcing its long-term commitment 
to one of the fastest-growing segments of the passenger vehicle market. At the same time, its multi-powertrain strategy 
continues to provide customers with a wide range of mobility choices suited to diverse needs and usage patterns.
The Company's multi-pathway approach, comprising Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles 
(SHEVs), CNG, Compressed Biogas (CBG), ethanol-compatible vehicles and flex-fuel technologies, reflects its belief that 
sustainable mobility must remain inclusive and aligned with India's unique needs. While e VITARA marked the Company's 
entry into the battery electric vehicle segment, it further strengthened its multi-powertrain portfolio with the introduction 
of the WagonR Flex Fuel Vehicle. Together, these initiatives underscore the Company's commitment to offering customers 
multiple pathways towards lower-carbon mobility.
Beyond products and markets, the Company continues to prepare for a rapidly evolving future. The automotive 
industry is undergoing a profound transformation driven by decarbonisation, software, artificial intelligence and 
advanced manufacturing technologies. At the same time, evolving geopolitical realities have highlighted the importance 
of complementing efficiency with resilience. The Company is strengthening localisation, investing in future-ready 
capabilities, expanding digital adoption and working closely with suppliers and other stakeholders to build a more 
resilient local supplier ecosystem.
'The Next Million, New Momentum' therefore represents more than a growth aspiration. It reflects the Company entering 
its next phase of growth with renewed confidence, multiple growth drivers, future-ready capabilities and a steadfast 
commitment to creating sustainable value for customers, society and the nation.

Company Profile
Maruti Suzuki India Limited was established in 1981. A joint venture agreement was signed between the Government of India and 
Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC), Japan in 1982. The Company became a subsidiary of SMC in 2002. In terms of production volume 
and sales, the Company is now SMC's largest subsidiary. As of 31st March 2026, SMC holds 58.53% of its equity stake. It is a public 
limited Company, and its shares are traded on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). The 
Company is the market leader of Passenger Vehicles (PVs) in India and is also the country’s largest exporter of PVs. In FY 2025-26, 
the Company posted its highest-ever total sales, surpassing the milestone of 2 million units for the third year in a row. The Company 
is the first among PV manufacturers in India to achieve this milestone.

Message from  the Chairman
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome all of you to this the 45th annual general meeting of Maruti Suzuki India Limited. As we have 
been doing in the past, and in accordance with the existing law and rules on the subject, the meeting is being held virtually. One clear 
benefit of this system is that it enables shareholders to participate, and ask questions, from any part of the world. Physical meetings 
would not enable this to happen unless outstation shareholders incurred substantial costs to travel and stay at the meeting place.
In the last AGM I expressed my optimism about the future of the car industry, and especially of small cars, after the Prime Minister’s 
announcement that the GST system would be reformed from September 22nd. This happened and I am happy to inform you that these 
reforms have given a new impetus not only to the automobile industry but to several sectors of the economy. National GDP growth 
figures since then have been better than were forecast by most agencies. Despite the Iran-US war, that has adversely affected most 
global economies, the Indian economy continues to do well and remains the fastest growing among larger countries. GST collections, 
despite rates of tax being reduced on over 90% of products, have shown buoyancy and reached new high levels. I believe that without 
GST reforms we may not have done so well in the difficult months that have elapsed. On behalf of all of you I would like to convey our 
humble congratulations to the Prime Minister, the finance minister and all other members of the government. 
I would urge the government, including the State governments, to proceed faster on the road of reforms. Increase efforts to make 
doing business easier. Use more technology as it has shown that it reduces corruption and delays. Time saving is a major factor in 
lowering costs of production. Trust the private sector and the power of competition. Faster creation of wealth, in the most efficient 
manner, is the only way that India can make up for the time that we have lost. This has been demonstrated by the automobile sector. 
Large employment opportunities have opened up in the economy due to the growth of a competitive automobile industry. My request 
to all political parties is to support reforms and programmes that create wealth. The government, and the opposition, should ensure 
that the additional resources that would be generated would be used to create a more equitable and just society.
The financial year 2025-26 was a record year for your company. We achieved the highest level of sales of 24.22 lakh vehicles, highest 
exports of 4.47 lakh cars, highest production of 23.4 lakh cars and highest consolidated revenues of ` 1.83 lakh crores. The Annual 
profit at INR 14,445.4 crores was the highest ever. Our share price rose to ` 17,370 in January 2026 before the war brought down the 
entire market. As a result, your Board has been able to recommend a dividend of ` 140 on a share with face value of ` 5, the highest 
ever. This is consistent with the dividend policy and takes into account the massive investments being made by your company. I do 
hope you will support this recommendation. 
Overall, after the implementation of the new GST rates on the 22nd of September 2025, MSIL retail sales grew 17% in the second half 
of last year. We ended March with 1.9 lakh pending bookings, a result of inadequate manufacturing capacity of the models in demand. 
This was the consequence of adjustments made over the past several years to cater to the fall in small car sales and the growth of 
the SUV market. We are remedying this situation by making all our new production lines flexible enough to permit your company to 
change platforms and models as may be required. This is already showing results. In the first quarter of this year your company’s sales 
grew by 38%, while industry grew 28%. The sales of small cars grew 17% in the second half of last year but grew 35% in quarter 1 
this year as more cars required by customers could be produced. Your company is in the process of making as accurate an estimate 
as possible of the likely growth of the car market in the next five years, a happy exercise necessitated by the GST reforms. This could 
lead to some changes in our longer-term targets. Presently, we are estimating that the car industry would grow to 6.1 to 6.3 million by 
FY 2030-31 and that the share of the small car market would grow significantly faster than what had happened in the last five years. 
Your company has introduced an electric SUV, and it has been well received. 40,873 units of the EV have been exported so far and 
domestic sales during the first quarter were at 5,648. We have been comfortably meeting all the regulatory requirements and expect 
to continue to do so in the future.

CNG cars have been in much demand. In FY 2025-26 sales rose by 22% to 7.46 lakh cars. In the first quarter of this year we sold 2.2 
lakh CNG cars, a 58% growth. This year’s target is 9 lakh CNG cars.
Moving cars by using rail transport continues to be a priority activity. The percentage of cars sent by rail in FY 2025-26 was 26.5% 
and this number is expected to reach 28% in FY 2026-27. The railway siding in the Manesar plant is working well and resulting in 
cost saving and convenience. We will also have a similar siding in Kharkhoda. Rail transport also results in reducing the carbon load 
and has less risk of damage in transit. 
Your company now has almost a 50% share of the cars exported from India. Japan has become our third largest export market. 
Export volumes are targeted to increase from last year’s level, despite the problems in the middle east.
Two lines have been commissioned in Kharkhoda and work is progressing on the third line. A fourth line of 250,000 capacity was 
commissioned at Hansalpur, raising installed capacity to 1 million. This is Suzuki’s largest plant anywhere in the world. Work has 
started at a new site in Sanand in Gujarat, and it is intended to install a total capacity of 1 million units there. The proposed investment 
at the Sanand site is ` 35,000 crores. As a result of the expansion projects, our installed capacity would reach 2.9 million units at the 
end of FY 2026-27 and 3.65 million units at the end of FY 2030-31. 
Our economy has a huge potential for growth. The government is committed to taking the economy along a sustained high growth 
path. The automotive industry will follow as the ability to commute comfortably and safely is a constituent of a developed economy. 
Your company is planning ahead on how to continue to play a leadership role in the future. We have to take into account not only 
the implications of artificial intelligence but also, as good citizens, to ensure that we play our part in meeting all the requirements of 
environmental protection and safety. 
We have been working in this direction for many years now. Our carbon footprint in the production process would reduce from the 
present 615,000 tonnes to 266,000 tonnes in FY 2030-31. Renewable electricity would increase from the present 23% to 85% by 
FY 2030-31. Solar energy use by the company would rise from 79 MWp at the end of FY 2025-26 to 319 MWp by 2030-31, with 214 
MWp being generated in-house. We are also in the process of establishing biogas production inhouse to meet clean and renewable 
energy needs of the production process. By FY 2030-31 we intend to use over 20 tonnes of biogas per day. Water intensity in the 
production process is expected to decrease by 17% by FY 2030-31 compared to FY 2025-26. Gurgaon and Manesar have already 
been awarded water positive certificates, and we will also get these certificates for Kharkhoda and Hansalpur.
Your company has always maintained that in India we need to use multiple technologies to achieve our goal of moving to net zero. We 
strongly believe that biogas can be generated in large quantities from locally available resources. This form of energy would substitute 
for imported CNG and be clean and renewable with zero import content. In addition, there would be many valuable byproducts. 
Fermented organic manure, produced in the process, would not only increase the productivity of land but also improve soil quality. 
Crop burning could be avoided and that would not only help a cleaner environment but would also prevent harm to the soil microbes. 
The income of farmers would increase, and mechanization of harvesting and field preparation would be promoted. Your company 
has been working with the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Pusa over the last two years and the preliminary report is consistent 
with what I have said. The government has just announced a scheme called GOBARdhan to promote compressed biogas production.
Your Board has approved that we start four biogas plants in the 1st phase, at a cost of ` 561 crores, and once we have learnt more 
about the process and technology, we hope to invest substantial amounts of money in the production and distributions of biogas. It 
will provide zero emission fuel and reduce the pressure on CNG and on burning coal for generating electricity.
Our emphasis on constantly improving customer satisfaction and convenience remains unchanged. The sales of cars in rural areas 
are growing faster than in urban areas, and we are accordingly implementing the expansion of sales, service and spare part outlets. 
Last year we added 868 new sales and service touchpoints, bringing the total to 10,527. Your company is making all possible efforts 
to learn about what customers want by commissioning market surveys and also keeping in touch on this aspect with our dealers 
and field staff. 
The basic policy relating to CSR continues without change. Your company has been spending the CSR budget in full every year 
including FY 2025-26. The strategy for supporting improvement in skills training has been modified and we now only adopt those 
ITI’s where the State government concerned gives us a free hand to align the equipment, syllabus and training system with the needs 
of modern manufacturing. The work of improving villages around all our facilities continues and is being expanded. The road safety 
programme is much in demand. 
Your company’s strength continues to be the entire Maruti team as well as our vendor and dealer partners. It has been established 
beyond doubt that the stronger the teamwork between all employees and other partners, the better would be the results. A car 
manufacturing company cannot succeed by individual contributions, however talented these individuals may be. Teamwork would 
always produce superior results. Your management intends to pursue this line of thinking and work accordingly.
Your company continues to attach high importance to safety of both our facilities and our people. We have extended support in these 
areas for our vendors. I am happy to report that the continuous emphasis on safety and hygiene is gradually changing the behaviour 
pattern of employees who are becoming more safety conscious. The number of fatalities in accidents in our plants in FY 2025-26 
were nil. 
During the year our working with Suzuki, Japan has become closer and more integrated. Both sides realise that our competitiveness 
can be maximized by continually strengthening the partnership between the two companies, while of course taking care to see that 
we do not violate any of the laws relating to transactions that have to be at arm’s length. I would like to acknowledge with gratitude, 
the help and support of the President of Suzuki Motor Corporation, T. Suzuki San in taking us forward. In particular, we are working 
closer than ever to strength our capacity for building new models of cars in shorter and more cost-effective ways. Engineering strength 
is the core value that leads to success of a car company.
I would like to place my deep appreciation for the support that I have received from the Board, all employees and our vendor and 
dealer partners.
With these words I thank you once again for all the cooperation we have received from all of you and wish you all another safe and 
prosperous year ahead.
Jai Hind.

Message from the 
Managing Director and CEO
It is my privilege to share our journey and future thoughts through this Integrated Report
At Maruti Suzuki, my personal mission is simple, which is to bring the Joy of Mobility to as many people as possible.
Mobility is not merely about transportation. It enables people to access opportunities, improve their quality of life, participate more 
actively in the economy and pursue their aspirations with greater confidence. For mobility to deliver its full social and economic value, 
it must be inclusive and equitable. It should reach first-time buyers, young families, rural customers, urban professionals and aspiring 
households alike. This belief has guided Maruti Suzuki since its inception and continues to shape our decisions today
In that context, FY 2025–26 gave us a new momentum towards my mission
One of the most encouraging developments during FY 2025–26 was the revival of the small car segment led by GST reduction. Small 
cars have historically democratised mobility in India and have served as the first step into car ownership for millions of families. Their 
recovery is important not only for the automobile industry, but also for expanding access to safer and more comfortable mobility across 
society. I believe mobility has its greatest impact when it empowers people in their everyday lives.
On one hand small cars signaled the return of a broader consumer base and on the other hand SUV portfolio was strengthened with the 
launch of Victoris and e Vitara. As a result, we could achieve highest-ever sales volume in domestic market in FY 2025-26. 
Another notable highlight of FY 2025–26 was the continued strength of exports despite an increasingly dynamic geopolitical environment. 
By leveraging Suzuki’s global distribution network, today Maruti Suzuki vehicles are sold in nearly 120 countries. This broad geographical 
presence has reduced dependence on any single region and strengthened business resilience. 
Exports will continue to play an important role in our future growth strategy. With the commencement of exports of e VITARA, we are 
re-entering advanced markets such as Europe and Japan while further strengthening India's position within Suzuki's global operations. 
This reinforces our long-standing commitment to the vision of 'Make in India, Make for the World.'
During FY 2025-26, the Company achieved several significant milestones. Annual production exceeded 2 million units for the second 
consecutive year, and annual sales reached a record 2.42 million vehicles, including the highest-ever export volume of 447,774 vehicles. 
In FY 2025-26, Maruti Suzuki alone contributed to nearly 50% of overall Passenger Vehicles exported from India. The Company remained 
India's leading exporter of passenger vehicles for the fifth consecutive year. Revenue increased to an all-time high of over INR 1.8 lakh 
crore, with profit after tax about ` 144,454 million also reaching record levels. Consequently, the Board has recommended highest-
ever dividend of ` 140 per share. The Company expresses its sincere gratitude to all stakeholders for their contributions towards these 
notable achievements.
The theme of this year's Integrated Report, "The Next Million, New Momentum – Every Engine of Growth in Motion," reflects the inflection 
point in our journey. Today, with multiple growth engines moving simultaneously, the journey towards next million sales milestone appears 
significantly faster than previously anticipated.
Reflecting our confidence in the medium-term outlook, we accelerated our capacity expansion plans. During FY 2026–27, we added 
500,000 units of manufacturing capacity. 
Customer expectations continue to evolve rapidly. The Company has plans to introduce 7 SUVs in the next 5 years to further strengthen 
SUV portfolio. Beyond mobility, customers increasingly seek safety, comfort, convenience and connectivity.
Safety remains at the core of our product philosophy. We democratised safety technologies such as six airbags and ESC and offered 
them as a standard across nearly the entire portfolio in the domestic market. During the year, our commitment to safer mobility received 
strong validation through the achievement of 5-Star Bharat NCAP safety ratings in Victoris and e VITARA. Such recognition reinforces 
our belief that advanced safety technologies should progressively become accessible to a wider section of customers and contribute 
towards making Indian roads safer. 
During FY 2025–26, e VITARA, Company’s first Battery Electric Vehicle, marked a significant milestone in our technology journey. It is a 
matter of pride that Maruti Suzuki will serve as the exclusive global production hub for this vehicle within the Suzuki Group. This reinforces 
the growing strategic importance of India in Suzuki's global manufacturing and technology roadmap.

At the same time, we recognise that the transition to electric mobility requires much more than launching a vehicle. Building customer 
confidence requires the creation of a reliable and convenient ecosystem around EV ownership. Accordingly, we continue to strengthen 
EV readiness across our ecosystem through an expanding charging infrastructure, EV-ready service workshops and partnerships with 
charge point operators. Our focus remains on making electric mobility practical, convenient and accessible to customers
However, for a country as large and diverse as India, no single technology pathway can adequately address all mobility needs.
Therefore, our approach remains centered around a multi-pathway strategy comprising Battery Electric Vehicles, Strong Hybrid Electric 
Vehicles, CNG, Compressed Biogas (CBG), E20-compatible vehicles and Flex Fuel technologies. We believe such an approach offers 
the most practical pathway towards carbon reduction while preserving affordability, customer choice, energy security and suitability to 
local conditions. By pursuing multi-powertrain approach, we could achieve our CAFE (Phase-2) target for FY 2025-26 by a good margin.
Among these pathways, I am excited about the opportunities presented by biofuels and Compressed Biogas (CBG) in particular.
India possesses abundant biomass resources, creating a significant opportunity to produce low-carbon fuel domestically. Beyond 
reducing emissions, CBG has the potential to simultaneously strengthen energy atmanirbharta by reducing dependence on imported 
fossil fuels and supply chain atmanirbharta by creating local value chains and supporting rural economy. CBG also helps to improve air 
quality in urban areas as it uses paddy straw as a feedstock, thereby reducing crop burning. The increasing importance being accorded 
to biogas, including during recent engagements between the Prime Ministers of India and Japan, reinforces its strategic relevance for 
the future.
Technology is also transforming the Company in ways that go well beyond vehicle powertrains.
The rapid rise of software content in vehicles and the advances being made in Artificial Intelligence, particularly Generative AI, are 
fundamentally reshaping product development, manufacturing, quality management, safety improvement and customer experience. 
As we scale up, digital technologies are becoming indispensable for improving efficiency, enabling faster and more informed decision-
making, and enhancing organisational agility. Across Maruti Suzuki, we are increasingly leveraging digital technologies. 
As we embrace these opportunities, we remain conscious of emerging risks.
The automotive industry today operates not only in a more interconnected but also more uncertain world. The increasing adoption 
of advanced technologies is also leading to greater dependence on specialised materials, semiconductors, batteries and electronic 
components, supply chains for which remain concentrated in a limited number of countries.
Recent geopolitical developments, including the conflict in West Asia, have highlighted the vulnerability of global supply chains and 
reinforced the need to balance efficiency with resilience.
Localisation, alternate sourcing, supplier capability development and ecosystem development remain critical priorities. Our objective 
is not merely to mitigate risk but to strengthen India's long-term competitiveness in future mobility technologies.
Sustainability remains integral to our business strategy.
For us, sustainability is not a separate agenda. It is embedded in the way we design products, operate factories, manage resources 
and engage with stakeholders. Our efforts span the entire vehicle lifecycle, from product development and manufacturing to logistics, 
usage and end-of-life management.
We continue to improve resource efficiency and reduce energy demand by adopting Suzuki’s core philosophy of Sho-Sho-Kei-Tan-Bi, 
which translates to smaller, lighter, fewer, shorter and more beautiful.  At the same time, we are transitioning towards clean energy driven 
by renewable electricity and increasing use of biogas as a process fuel. The Company has plans to expand capacity of solar power 
generation from 79.2 MWp to 319 MWp by FY 2030-31. Besides, to maximise the use of renewable power we procure green power from 
external sources and use Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) having a capacity of 1 MWh. By 2027, capacity of in-plant biogas plant 
will increase to 10.7 TPD from 0.7 TPD.  The Company continues to increasingly adopt rail-based logistics to reduce logistics-related 
emissions. 
During the year, the Company further strengthened ESG practices across its value chain by promoting renewable energy adoption, 
responsible sourcing and robust governance standards among suppliers and dealer partners. It also continued to enforce global 
standards on the management of Substances of Concern (SoC), conducting over 470 supplier assessments and awareness programmes 
to drive compliance and capability enhancement.
The Company remains committed to building a responsible and resilient value chain. Cumulatively, human resource systems and 
human rights practices were assessed for local Tier-1 suppliers accounting for 84% of component purchases by value. In addition, the 
Company continued to promote occupational health and safety, skill development and governance excellence across its ecosystem. 
During FY 2025–26, over 2,550 training programmes were conducted covering 100% of Tier-1 suppliers and dealer partners, while a 
comprehensive governance framework was extended across all Tier-1 suppliers to strengthen transparency, risk management, ethical 
conduct and sustainable value creation.
One of the greatest strengths of Maruti Suzuki is its culture of partnership and participation. The growth of our employees and the growth 
of the Company have always been intrinsically linked. During FY 2025–26, employees contributed more than 1.8 million suggestions 
aimed at improving safety, quality, productivity and cost competitiveness. This remarkable achievement reflects a deeply embedded 
culture of ownership, continuous improvement and shared success.
With pace of technological change accelerating and workforce getting younger, preserving the values and culture that have shaped our 
success while building future-ready capabilities remains a strategic priority. The technologies of the future can be acquired and developed. 
Values and culture take decades to build. Sustaining these foundations while preparing the organisation for future opportunities will 
remain one of our most important responsibilities.
The CSR initiatives continue to progress as guided by the Board. Through the CSR programmes, the Company continues to create a 
positive impact on the lives of the people in the areas of community development, road safety and skill development. 
The Company undertakes community development initiatives near its facilities, focusing on healthcare, education, sanitation, and 
infrastructure. Its multispecialty hospital and Podar Learn School in Sitapur, Gujarat, both in their fifth year of operation, have served 
over 150,000 patients and provided quality education to local students. The Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) initiative, undertaken in 
collaboration with agricultural and research institutions, expanded across nine states to evaluate its potential and promote sustainable 
farming practices among over 200,000 farmers.
On road safety, the Company has trained over 5.5 million people over the last 25 years and established 86 automated driving test tracks 
in partnership with the transport departments of Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, 
Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. These tracks use computer vision systems and AI-based technology to assess driving 
skills transparently and efficiently before the issuance of driving licenses.
In skill development, the Company is working towards creating livelihood opportunities for Indian youth by imparting training in relevant 
skills through the Japan India Institutes for Manufacturing (JIM) set up by the Company and by supporting 144 Industrial Training Institutes 
(ITIs) nationwide. Over 19,600 students were trained in FY 2025-26. This programme aligns with the Government of India’s Skill India 
initiative.
Finally, as India progresses towards becoming a developed nation by 2047, the automobile industry has both a responsibility and 
an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to this journey. Through manufacturing, exports, technology development, employment 
generation, skill creation and sustainable mobility, Maruti Suzuki remains committed to supporting India's aspirations.
The next million vehicles represent far more than a volume milestone. They represent greater access to mobility, stronger manufacturing 
capabilities, wider adoption of cleaner technologies, deeper localisation and broader value creation for society.
I firmly believe that the momentum created during FY 2025–26 positions us well for the opportunities ahead.
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to our shareholders, customers, employees, suppliers, dealers, logistics partners, government 
authorities and all other stakeholders for their continued trust and support.
Together, we will continue our efforts to expand the Joy of Mobility and create sustainable value for society and future generations.

Average Fleet CO2 Emissions –

The Company’s average fleet carbon emission is significantly 
lower than the targeted industry average. Besides, the 
Company has been achieving its CAFE target by a good 
margin, across both Phase 1 (2017-18 to 2021-22) and Phase 2 
(Ongoing since 2022-23).
Maximising Decarbonisation 
through a Multi-powertrain Strategy
The Company is fully committed to supporting India’s goal of 
achieving Net Zero carbon emissions by 2070. Reduction in overall 
carbon emissions cannot be achieved unless the entire fleet of 
vehicles contributes to decarbonisation efforts. Accordingly, 
the Company’s strategy is to deploy multiple technologies so 
that every vehicle in the fleet contributes to reducing carbon 
emissions.
The car industry requires solutions that are scalable and 
affordable to reduce carbon emissions across the entire fleet. 
In addition to Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), the Company has 
adopted a multi-powertrain strategy comprising Strong Hybrid 
Electric Vehicles (SHEVs) and vehicles powered by alternative 
fuels, including Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and biofuels 
such as Compressed Biogas (CBG) and ethanol, to maximise its 
decarbonisation objectives.
In line with Suzuki’s mid-term plan for its India operations for 
FY 2030-31, BEVs are projected to account for 15% of the 
domestic PV sales volume, 25% from SHEVs, 35% from CNG 
and 25% from gasoline blended with biofuels.

Efforts towards Electrification of Powertrain
A. Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV)
The Company marked its entry into the Battery Electric Vehicle 
(BEV) segment in India with the introduction of the e VITARA in 
FY 2025-26. The e VITARA is Suzuki Motor Corporation’s first BEV 
offering, and the Company will serve as the global manufacturing 
hub for the entire Suzuki Group, with plans to export the vehicle 
to over 100 countries, providing a significant boost to the ‘Make 
in India’ initiative.

by a fast-charging network, with over 1,600 EV-ready service 
centres and specially trained personnel, including NEXA EV 
Relationship Managers and dedicated Charging Managers, to 
facilitate a seamless ownership experience.

the Indian market, along with establishing a charging network of 
over 1 lakh charging points by FY 2030-31.

packs for more than one million vehicles and currently has a

Broad Overview of Biogas Production at Manesar Facility
B. Increasing Use of Renewable Process Fuels
Use of Biofuel – Generating Compressed Biogas from Food Waste
The Company undertook initiatives in FY 2025-26 to increase the 
capacity of the biogas plant at its Manesar facility. In FY 2024-25, 
the Company had set up a pilot biogas project at Manesar using 
in-house food waste and Napier grass as resources.
The pilot project had a capacity of 0.2 Tonnes Per Day (TPD) that 
was scaled up to 0.7 TPD in FY 2025-26, marking another step in 
the Company’s commitment to sustainable manufacturing.
The Company is in process of setting up a 10 TPD biogas plant 
at its Kharkhoda facility, which is expected to be commissioned 
by 2027.
Aligned with the Government’s broader ‘waste to wealth’ 
philosophy, the facility utilises paddy straw as feedstock, 
with a provision to enhance output through the use of cattle 
dung. It leverages anaerobic digestion technology to convert 
agricultural waste into raw biogas. The plant is expected to 
generate approximately 2.6 lakh standard cubic metres of biogas 
annually, resulting in an estimated avoidance of 474 tonnes of CO₂ 
emissions per year.
The plant’s biogas can be utilised in paint shop heating processes 
as well as in canteen operations. Fermented Organic Manure 
(FOM), a by-product of the process, will be used for internal 
horticulture or supplied back to the agricultural ecosystem.

External Environment
External Environment
Strategic Response
The Company continues to pursue a multi-powertrain 
strategy comprising BEVs, SHEVs, CNG, Compressed 
Biogas (CBG) and ethanol-compatible vehicles. The 
Company believes a multi-pathway decarbonisation 
approach will maximise carbon reduction, enable 
customers to choose solutions best suited to their needs, 
diversify technology risks and support long-term business 
resilience and financial health.
Recognising that product use accounts for the majority 
of a vehicle's lifecycle emissions, the Company remains 
focused on reducing emissions through multiple powertrain 
technologies. At the same time, it is pursuing greenhouse 
gas reduction opportunities across the value chain, 
including manufacturing operations, energy consumption, 
logistics and the supplier ecosystem. 
India's economy remained resilient during FY 2025-26, 
despite geopolitical uncertainty, trade disruptions and 
commodity volatility.  GST reduction on cars improved 
affordability and revived participation from first-time 
buyers, particularly in the small car segment, a key driver 
of sustained industry growth.
Geopolitical developments continue to create uncertainty 
around commodity prices, energy costs, logistics networks 
and supply chain stability. Besides, geopolitical tensions 
and the emergence of tariff barriers pose risks to global 
trade and market access. 
Increasing acceptance of India-manufactured vehicles 
and recently concluded Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) 
with key markets such as the UK and EU are creating new 
opportunities for automotive exports. These developments 
are strengthening India's position as a global automotive 
manufacturing hub and expanding the growth potential of 
the automotive industry. 
India's low passenger vehicle penetration, rising incomes 
and increasing aspirations for personal mobility continue 
to provide substantial growth opportunities for the industry. 
Climate change continues to reshape the automotive 
industry globally. The pace and nature of the mobility 
transition is expected to vary across markets depending 
on economic conditions, infrastructure readiness and 
resource availability.
Several emerging powertrain technologies are yet to 
achieve the level of cost competitiveness required for 
widespread adoption in a price-sensitive market such 
as India. In addition, supply chains for certain critical 
materials remain concentrated, creating potential cost and 
availability risks.
For India, balancing carbon reduction with affordability, 
accessibility and suitability to local resource conditions 
remains critical. Consequently, Battery Electric Vehicles 
(BEVs), Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles (SHEVs), CNG, 
biofuels and other low-carbon technologies are expected 
to complement one another in reducing emissions. 
The global automotive industry is undergoing a once-in-
a-century transformation, resulting in a rapidly evolving 
regulatory landscape. Accordingly, the regulatory 
environment in India is shaping up.
Given the breadth of the Company's product portfolio and 
powertrain offerings, regulatory compliance is resource-
intensive. The sudden regulatory changes and non-tariff 
barriers have the potential to influence market access and 
export competitiveness. 
India's growing importance as the world's third-largest 
passenger vehicle market is expected to intensify competition 
and accelerate innovation across the industry.
With annual passenger vehicle sales approaching 5 million 
units, India has emerged as one of the world's most important 
automotive markets. Continued economic growth, rising 
incomes and favourable demographic trends are expected 
to further enhance its attractiveness for both domestic and 
global automotive players. 
Importantly, the Company believes that a changing 
competitive landscape ultimately benefits customers 
by driving innovation, improving product offerings and 
enhancing overall value. 
Strategic Response
To mitigate near-term risks, the Company continues to 
focus on cost optimisation, localisation, strengthening 
supply chain resilience, developing alternate sources of 
supply and expanding its supplier base.
Reflecting confidence in long-term domestic and 
export opportunities, the Company increased its annual 
production capacity from approximately 2.4 million units 
to 2.9 million units during FY 2026-27 and remains on 
course to achieve its medium-term objective of expanding 
annual production capacity to 4 million units. Supported by 
Suzuki Motor Corporation's global network and diversified 
presence across international markets, exports are 
expected to remain an important pillar of the Company's 
long-term growth strategy. 
Strategic Response
Access to Suzuki Motor Corporation's technological 
capabilities remains a critical enabler for timely regulatory 
compliance across domestic and international markets. 
Simultaneously, the Company continues to strengthen 
its engineering, testing and regulatory preparedness 
capabilities through investments in advanced infrastructure 
and the Rohtak R&D facility. These efforts enhance its 
ability to meet evolving regulations while continuing 
to deliver safe, efficient and technologically advanced 
mobility solutions.
Strategic Response
The Company continues to strengthen its competitiveness 
through product portfolio expansion, localisation, 
manufacturing excellence and access to advanced 
technologies through Suzuki Motor Corporation. Ongoing 
investments in product development, safety, quality and 
customer experience are aimed at sustaining long-term 
competitiveness in an evolving market environment.

Competitive Landscape
The Indian passenger vehicle market is simultaneously 
witnessing the revival of affordable mobility and 
continued premiumisation. While demand for small 
cars has improved, SUVs continue to account for 
a significant share of industry volumes. In today’s 
digitally connected world, customer expectations 
are evolving rapidly. New-age buyers seek premium 
styling, advanced technology, enhanced comfort and 
convenience, and connected features. 
Growing preference for CNG, hybrid and electric 
vehicles, rising demand for Advanced Driver Assistance 
Systems (ADAS), and increasing expectations around 
connected features and digital experiences are 
reshaping product development priorities across the 
industry.
Strategic Response
The Company continues to broaden its portfolio across vehicle 
segments and powertrain technologies. The Company has 
plans to launch 7 SUVs in the next 5 years. Investments in safety, 
connectivity, convenience features and multiple powertrain 
options are aimed at meeting evolving customer expectations. 
The Company is also expanding the availability of advanced 
technologies such as ADAS, connected vehicle solutions and 
digital interfaces across its portfolio while maintaining a strong 
focus on affordability and customer value.
To improve the affordability and scalability of emerging 
technologies, the Company is accelerating localisation through 
advanced development initiatives and undertaking focused 
value engineering and value analysis activities. These efforts 
support wider adoption of advanced technologies while 
preserving customer value.

Risk Management
The Company understands that effective risk management is critical in meeting its strategic objectives and achieving sustainable 
growth. It has a structured risk management process, which is overseen by the Risk Management Committee. This Committee 
monitors and reviews the Company’s risk management plan as per relevant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, and Listing 
Regulations. Accountability for the mitigation of each risk is assigned to the identified risk owners.
The Company applied the net risk principle to determine its risks. The top management monitors mitigation measures to counter 
these risks. If the following risks manifest, they have negative implications.

Circularity Management
In a first-of-its-kind initiative to transition from a linear to circular 
material flow model, Maruti Suzuki has operationalised a 
closed-loop material circularity framework for ferrous (Steel) 
and non-ferrous (Aluminium) scrap generated at its plants. The 
Company's closed-loop model strengthens material circularity 
and contributes to emissions reduction.
Material Circularity 
Supply chain operations are one of the major contributors 
to the Company’s overall GHG emissions (Scope 3.1). Steel 
and aluminium are the two major materials. Therefore, 
decarbonisation of the supply chain remains a key enabler in the 
Company’s journey towards Carbon Neutrality.
Steel scrap and aluminium scrap generated during vehicle 
manufacturing are routed to approved raw material suppliers 
for recycling into alloy steel grades and aluminium ingots, thus 
establishing a closed-loop circularity system. This initiative is 
estimated to reduce GHG emissions with steel and aluminium 
recycling through logistics optimisation to reduce dependency 
on imported scrap.
Benefits of Material Circularity
1.	 Resource Efficiency: Internal reuse of scrap 
from press, casting and machining shops reduces 
dependency on virgin and imported raw materials
2.	 Raw Material Security: Closed-loop local 
recycling secures a consistent supply of recycled 
metal, reducing vulnerability to global supply chain 
disruptions
3.	 GHG Emission Reduction: Supply chain 
optimisation through scrap circularity reduces 
greenhouse gas emissions across the value chain

Environmental Sustainability in Products
As a responsible manufacturer, the Company remains at the forefront of India's passenger vehicle market. The Company continues to 
drive innovation and demonstrate strategic agility in areas such as electrification, sustainability, carbon neutrality, and next-generation 
mobility solutions, while responding to intensifying competition from both domestic and global players.
New Products
The Company continues to pursue a multi-powertrain strategy 
comprising BEVs, SHEVs, CNG, Compressed Biogas (CBG) 
and ethanol-compatible vehicles. The Company believes a 
multi-pathway decarbonisation approach will maximise carbon 
reduction, enable customers to choose solutions best suited to 
their needs and diversify technology risks. 
Introducing Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV)
The Company launched an electric SUV - e VITARA marking a 
transformative milestone in India’s electric mobility journey. The 
Company is expected to launch four EV models by FY 2030-
31. The Company is working to create a robust electric vehicle 
ecosystem with comprehensive end-to-end digital platform, the 
‘e for Me’ app, for EV charging needs, including home charging 
and public charging with an integrated payment journey. Over 
2000 exclusive charging points will be available to customers 
across the nationwide dealer network. The Company will work 
with partners to enable over 100,000 public charging points by 
2030.
CNG
Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) remains a key environment-
friendly pillar in the Company’s  mobility portfolio, offering its 
customers a lower-emissions transportation alternative with 
enhanced fuel economy that incurs lower operating cost. The 
Company currently offers CNG technology across 14 models 
and commands nearly three-fourths of the market share of CNG 
vehicles in the industry.
Hybrid
In parallel, the Company continues to promote its Hybrid 
technology portfolio by offering Smart Hybrid (Mild Hybrid) and 
Strong Hybrid. Smart Hybrid Technology enhances fuel efficiency 
and reduces dependence on conventional IC engines through 
electric motor assistance whereas, Strong Hybrid engines enable 
switching to an electric-only driving mode contributing to lower 
tailpipe emissions.
CBG
The Company is committed to explore sustainable mobility, 
Maruti Suzuki continues to advance a multi-pathway approach 
toward reducing carbon emissions. Recognising the significant 
potential of Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG) in India's energy 
transition, the Company has identified CBG as a strategic fuel that 
complements its strong CNG vehicle portfolio while supporting 
the Company's overall environmental objectives.
The Company continues to evaluate advancements in flex-fuel 
vehicle technology to support cleaner and more sustainable 
mobility solutions.
Designed for End-of-Life
The Company vehicles are designed in accordance with the 
minimum 85% Recyclability and 95% Recoverability requirements 
calculated through International Material Data System (IMDS) 
following ISO 22628, to assess material composition and 
end-of-life performance, thereby supporting responsible 
resource recovery. The average recyclability for the products 
manufactured by the Company is 92% and recoverability is 95%.
The Company also shared its perspective on reducing greenhouse gas emissions within India's passenger car sector, 
introducing the 'Clean for Life Vehicles' (CLV) concept as part of the GHG reduction framework.

Anaemia Reduction
Building on the learnings from earlier pilot interventions on 
anaemia reduction, the Company scaled up and strengthened 
its Anaemia Reduction Project during the reporting period. The 
project was designed to complement public healthcare systems 
by focusing on preventive care, early diagnosis and behaviour 
change, particularly among women, adolescent girls and 
children.
During the reporting period, the project was implemented across 
10 villages. A systematic approach was adopted to ensure 
comprehensive coverage, beginning with community‑level 
mobilisation and haemoglobin screening camps. These camps 
enabled early identification and classification of anaemia 
cases into mild, moderate and severe categories, allowing for 
timely medical intervention and referral wherever required.

Skill Development Projects 
The Company has taken up well-established vocational skill 
development programmes. In its endeavour to promote skill 
development, the Company adopts a two-pronged approach to 
enhance the capabilities of individuals and create a skilled and 
industry-ready workforce. Through the first approach, the Company 
has established the new vocational training Institutes, Japan India 
Institute for Manufacturing (JIM), to provide comprehensive training, 
incorporating theoretical knowledge and practical experience. The 
second approach focuses on improving the infrastructure and 
capacity of trainers of existing Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) to 
provide a conducive learning environment for students, equipped 
with modern tools and equipment necessary for skill development 
required for the industry. In addition to establishing skill training 
centres and supporting existing government ITIs, the Company 
actively implements apprenticeship and internship programmes 
aimed at enhancing employability among ITI pass-outs and 
graduates. These initiatives provide hands-on industry exposure, 
mentorship, and practical experience, bridging the gap between 
classroom learning and workplace requirements. By integrating 
these programmes into its CSR strategy, the Company reinforces 
its commitment to nurture a skilled and job-ready workforce.
Japan India Institute for Manufacturing 
Japan India Institute for Manufacturing (JIM) is a flagship skill 
development initiative that offers vocational training aligned with 
advanced manufacturing requirements. It reflects the collaborative 
efforts between the Governments of India and Japan to promote 
skill development and excellence in the manufacturing sector. 
During the reporting period, over 300 students were trained 
across JIMs, taking the cumulative number to approximately 
2,300+ students since inception. Through short-term courses, 
over 2,800 individuals were trained during the reporting period. 
The Company has established four JIMs - two in Gujarat and two 
in Haryana, with JIM Sonipat commencing admissions for its first 
batch during the reporting period. The overall capacity of JIMs was 
further enhanced to accommodate a larger number of students.
JIMs are affiliated under NCVET (National Council for Vocational 
Education and Training) and accredited by the Ministry of Economy, 
trade and Industry (METI), Japan. JIMs follow the Dual System 
of Training (DST), combining classroom instruction with industry 
exposure. Students undergo seven months of paid industry 
training annually, enabling practical experience and 'Earn While 
You Learn' opportunities, thereby strengthening their transition 
to the workforce.
JIMs provide training in advanced manufacturing techniques and 
efficient shop floor practices based on Japanese manufacturing 
principles, along with essential soft skills to improve employability. 
The institutes are equipped with state‑of‑the‑art infrastructure, 
including mini‑vehicle assembly lines, engine assembly lines, 
safety labs, welding and painting simulators, full‑fledged paint 
booths, robotics‑enabled systems and body repair facilities. During 
the year, welding robots were installed at JIM Manesar and Sonipat 
and Electric Vehicle (EV) training equipment was introduced at JIM 
Mehsana, strengthening future‑ready skill development.
Infrastructure development continued with the start of construction 
of student hostel facilities at JIM Sonipat and Manesar to support 
residential training needs. JIMs achieved a 100% pass percentage, 
with six students securing state‑level top ranks.

Compliance Management
Compliance continues to be a fundamental pillar of Maruti 
Suzuki’s governance framework. The Company remains 
committed to maintaining a robust and forward-looking 
compliance architecture aligned with evolving regulatory 
expectations and leading industry practices. The Company had 
proactively benchmarked its Compliance practices with best-in-

including operationalising the Compliance Committee. During the 
year, this commitment was further reinforced through quarterly 
meetings of the Compliance Committee comprising of senior 
business and compliance leaders, chaired by the Managing 
Director and CEO, Mr. H. Takeuchi. The strengthened governance 
structure has enhanced oversight of compliance risks, improved 
visibility at the senior management level, and facilitated the timely 
and effective implementation of compliance initiatives across the 
organisation.
The seamless integration of Suzuki Motor Gujarat (SMG) into the 
Company’s operations has been executed with a strong focus on 
regulatory alignment and reinforcement of a unified compliance 
culture. The integration process ensured that SMG’s operations 
are fully aligned with the Company’s established governance 
framework, policies, and applicable regulatory requirements. 
Through structured oversight, harmonisation of controls, and 
targeted compliance trainings, the Company has embedded 
consistent standards of ethical conduct, risk management, and 
statutory compliance across the integrated entity. This approach 
has strengthened overall compliance discipline, transparency, 
and accountability, while fostering a culture of integrity and 
adherence to regulatory expectations.
The Company is in full compliance with all applicable laws and 
regulations, including those governing labour, environmental, 
industrial, financial, IT, and corporate matters, as well as 
requirements under the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 as 
amended. Compliance certificates are submitted to the Board on 
a quarterly basis. To further strengthen monitoring and control, a 
Company-wide compliance e-monitoring tool was implemented 
during the reporting period. No significant instances of non-
compliance were reported during the year.
The Company marked its 10th Compliance Month in October 
2025, reaffirming its commitment to integrating compliance 
with business excellence. The Company continued to foster its 
culture of compliance through active leadership engagement, 
including participation by the Chairman, Mr. R C Bhargava, and 
the Managing Director and CEO, Mr. H. Takeuchi. This initiative 
was supported by structured awareness and training initiatives 
reinforcing compliance accountability across all levels of the 
organisation.

the Company enhanced its supplier engagement initiative through 
the 'Maruti Suzuki Supplier Corporate Governance Framework', 
aimed at promoting transparency, accountability, and adoption 
of corporate governance best practices across the value chain.

been adopted by 90% of its suppliers, reflecting the Company’s 
commitment to responsible and sustainable business practices.

Survey (R 5.18) with full employee participation, enabling 
assessment of ground-level awareness and implementation of

without hesitation. Insights from the survey have led to targeted 
interventions to strengthen the compliance framework and

are placing increased responsibility and

Tone from the Top during the Compliance Month
The Management continues to set a strong tone at the top, 
emphasising zero tolerance towards any form of misconduct. 
During the year, the Company further strengthened its outreach 
by extending POSH sensitisation to shop floor employees and 
contract workforce. In total, over 27,000 employees and workers 
were covered under these awareness initiatives. In accordance 
with statutory requirements, Internal Committees have been duly 
constituted across business verticals and locations to address 
complaints in a fair, impartial, and time-bound manner. These 
Committees are supported through regular training and capacity-
building initiatives to ensure continued effectiveness and alignment 
with evolving regulatory expectations. The Committees have 
complied with all statutory reporting requirements, including filing 
of annual returns. During the reporting period, two complaints 
were received and appropriately addressed in accordance with the 
prescribed procedures and timelines.
Demonstrating its commitment to transparent grievance redressal 
mechanisms, the Company has registered on the Government’s 
SHe-Box platform. The Company remains focused on enhancing 
diversity and inclusion, including increasing the participation of 
women in shop floor roles. At the end of the reporting period, 
over 190 women were employed on the shop floor. All requisite 
regulatory approvals have been obtained, and the Company 
ensures strict adherence to applicable safety measures for 
women working during night shifts, in accordance with relevant 
state regulations.
Whistle Blower Mechanism
The Company’s Whistle Blower Policy establishes a robust 
mechanism for employees to report concerns relating to unethical 
conduct, violations of the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics 
(COBCE), or any other irregularities, in a secure and confidential 
manner. The framework ensures accessibility of reporting channels 
and safeguards against any form of retaliation.
Complaints may be raised directly with the designated 
Ombudsperson or through the Company’s Complaint Committee. All 
concerns received are treated with due seriousness and are subject 
to a structured, impartial, and time-bound investigation process. 
During the reporting period, two complaints were received by the 
Ombudsperson and were duly noted by the Audit Committee of the 
Board. Any matter received by the ombudsperson is investigated 
by the complaint committee with the support of an independent 
external expert to ensure objectivity and rigour, if required. Based 
on the findings, appropriate actions are taken in accordance with 
the Company’s Disciplinary Policy.
Code of Business Conduct and 
Conflicts of Interest
The Company’s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (COBCE) 
establishes the foundation for ethical conduct and responsible 
decision-making across all business activities. Applicable to 
all white-collar employees, the COBCE outlines expectations 
relating to compliance with applicable laws, fair employment 
practices, stakeholder engagement, environmental stewardship, 
health and safety, conflicts of interest, data privacy, and 
protection of Company assets.
To ensure effective implementation, employees, including new 
hires, are regularly sensitised to COBCE and the Conflicts of 
Interest (COI) Policy through structured training programmes and 
ongoing awareness initiatives. Compliance is further reinforced 
through an annual affirmation process, whereby employees 
confirm adherence to COBCE and disclose any actual or potential 
conflicts of interest. In addition, the Company has in place duly 
certified Standing Orders governing the service conditions 
and conduct of its workforce. The Company also extends its 
commitment to high ethical standards across its value chain. 
Business associates and partners are expected to comply with all 
applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, including those 
relating to labour practices, prohibition of child labour, prevention 
of sexual harassment, environmental protection, and human 
rights. The Supplier Corporate Governance Council serves as 
a key platform for engagement with suppliers, facilitating both 
awareness-building and periodic assessment of compliance with 
critical statutory and governance requirements.
Prevention of Sexual Harassment
The Company is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, 
and respectful workplace, ensuring a safe and conducive 
environment free from all forms of harassment. A comprehensive 
Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) is in place 
in alignment with the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics 
(COBCE) and the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace 
(Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. The Policy 
provides a robust framework for the prevention, prohibition, 
and redressal of complaints, while ensuring confidentiality and 
protection of all concerned parties. All employees, including 
new hires, undergo mandatory POSH sensitisation at the time 
of induction and at regular intervals thereafter. These efforts are 
reinforced through ongoing awareness communications. 
Status of Compliances during FY 2025-26
Environmental Laws 
and Regulations
No non-compliance and significant sanctions (monetary or non-monetary) were imposed on the Company by the 
regulatory authorities. Emissions and waste generation were within the limits defined by the Pollution Control Board. 
As on 31st March 2026, satisfactory replies had been given to all showcause notices received from the Pollution 
Control Board.
Marketing 
Communications
No incidents of non-compliance. 
Advertising Standards
No complaints were filed.
Competition Law
Case Related to After-market Sale of Spare Parts
An investigation was initiated by the Competition Commission of India (CCI) in 2011 against a few car manufacturing 
companies wherein it was contended that these companies were not making genuine spare parts of automobiles 
freely available in the open market. CCI later expanded the scope of the investigation to other car manufacturing 
companies, including the Company. In the final order passed by the CCI on 25th August 2014, certain directions 
were laid down against the automobile companies and penalties were imposed. A penalty of ₹4,711.4 million was 
imposed on the Company. 
The Company contested this matter before the Delhi High Court primarily on the ground that it was not a named 
party in the investigation and that the investigation ought not to have been conducted against the Company. On the 
contrary, the Company was named in the information given by the informant as a Company that made spare parts 
easily accessible in the open market. The Delhi High Court, on 16th May 2019, disposed of the petition stating that 
the Company had alternative remedies available. Thereafter, the Company filed a Special Leave Petition before the 
Supreme Court of India, wherein a stay on the CCI’s order was granted, and the stay is continuing.
Matter Relating to Discount Control Practices
An investigation was initiated suo-moto by the CCI in February 2019 based on the information provided by a purported 
dealer of the Company. The dealer alleged that the Company resorts to anti-competitive discount control practices. 
The CCI passed its final order on 23rd August 2021 and held that the Company indulged in anti-competitive discount 
control practices (resale price maintenance) and imposed a penalty of ₹2,000 million on the Company. The Company 
filed an appeal against the order of the CCI before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), wherein 
on 22nd November 2021, a stay on the order of the CCI was granted subject to the deposit of ₹200 million. The stay 
is continuing.
Consumer Protection 
Laws
As on 31st March 2026, 2,061 consumer cases involving the Company were pending before various forums.

Information Security
Maruti Suzuki India Limited ('Maruti Suzuki') maintains a robust 
cyber security governance framework aligned with global 
standards and applicable regulatory requirements including 
the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. Guided by these 
requirements and international standards, the Company has 
established comprehensive information security policies, 
processes, and controls.
The Company is ISO 27001:2022 certified for Gurugram, 
Manesar, Head office, and Rohtak, with certification for the 
Kharkhoda and Hansalpur facilities successfully achieved during 
FY 2026-27. It operates under a comprehensive Information 
Security Management System (ISMS) Programme that governs 
cyber security risk management, data protection, and system 
resilience across the organisation.
The Company’s Information Security policy provides management 
direction and guidance to ensure availability, integrity and 
confidentiality of information and information systems across 
locations. Management Information Security Forum (MISF) 
has been constituted and is chaired by Managing Director and 
comprises the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and 
other senior management personnel. The MISF facilitates internal 
communication of information security programs, implements 
processes for risk assessment and security classification of 
information systems and reports critical security matters to the 
Board of Directors. The company is working towards AIS 189/190 
compliance to meet regulatory requirements for automotive 
cybersecurity and software update management, thereby 
supporting vehicle safety and reliability.
Data Protection
The Company is committed to upholding the privacy rights of 
its stakeholders and ensuring the protection of personal data 
through responsible data governance practices. In compliance 
with applicable data protection laws, including the Information 
Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection 
Rules, 2025, the Company is strengthening its data privacy 
framework and associated controls. These initiatives are aimed 
at ensuring regulatory compliance, enhancing data security, and 
fostering stakeholder trust.
The Company has set up a dedicated Data Protection Office and 
appointed a Data Protection Officer to manage the data privacy 
concerns. The Company has published the contact details of 
its Data Protection Officer on its website to serve as a point of 
contact for stakeholders and government authorities regarding 
queries, concerns, or requests pertaining to personal data 
protection and privacy.
The Company is progressively aligning its digital platforms with 
applicable data privacy regulations to ensure the protection of 
stakeholders' personal data. Employees are regularly educated 
on the Company's data protection policies and the evolving 
developments in data privacy laws through expert-led awareness 
sessions, e-learning modules, induction programmes for new 
hires and business advisories.
The Company continues to strengthen its data privacy framework 
through these initiatives, reaffirming its commitment to personal 
data protection, regulatory compliance, and responsible 
corporate governance.
Value Chain Governance 
Maruti Suzuki India Limited works with a vast and diverse 
supplier ecosystem comprising over 450 Tier-1 suppliers 
and nearly 1,500 Tier-2 suppliers. Recognising the critical 
role of strong governance in building a resilient, transparent, 
and sustainable value chain, Maruti Suzuki has adopted a 
structured approach to enhance governance standards across 
its supplier network.
In FY 2024-25, Maruti Suzuki, in collaboration with key supplier 
partners, launched the Supplier Corporate Governance 
Framework, an initiative designed to strengthen governance 
practices across the supply chain. The framework provides a 
structured mechanism for assessing and improving corporate 
governance standards among suppliers, fostering greater 
transparency, accountability and long-term value creation.
Building on the successful foundation established in 
FY 2024-25, the framework was expanded across the supplier 
ecosystem in FY 2025-26. Suppliers representing over 90% 
participation completed the governance self-assessment, 
demonstrating strong adoption and commitment from supplier 
partners. 
Supplier Code of Conduct
Maruti Suzuki has introduced a Supplier Code of Conduct (SCoC) 
built on transparency of expectations from its suppliers. The 
Code outlines clear expectations for suppliers and serves as a 
guiding framework to promote responsible business practices 
across the ecosystem. It reflects the Company's commitment 
to sustainability and integrity by embedding the core principles 
of environmental stewardship, social responsibility, responsible 
value chain management, compliance, and ethical conduct. 
Through this framework, the Company aims to strengthen 
supplier accountability and ensure consistency in operational 
and collaborative practices across its supplier ecosystem, while 
encouraging the adoption of similar standards and responsible 
business practices throughout the value chain.
Responsible Value Chain
The Company is committed to fostering a responsible and 
transparent value chain by promoting ethical sourcing practices 
across its supplier ecosystem. During the year, several initiatives 
were undertaken to strengthen supplier engagement and 
promote ethical procurement practices, including:
•	 Ethical sourcing and transparency by fostering 
responsible procurement practices across its supplier 
ecosystem.
•	 Awareness sessions on Conflict Minerals Reporting  
(Tin, Tantalum, Tungsten, Gold) conducted across Tier-1 
vendors.
•	 Introduction of structured suppliers’ self-assessment 
based on globally recognised CMRT (Conflict Minerals 
Reporting Template) for the first time.
Through the Supplier Corporate Governance Framework, 
Supplier Code of Conduct and the Supplier’s self-assessment 
on Conflict Mineral Reporting, Maruti Suzuki is contributing to 
a more responsible and sustainable supply chain ecosystem.
Intellectual Property (IP)
The Company recognises IP as a strategic business enabler of 
innovation and long-term value creation in today’s knowledge-
driven economy. Hence, as a part of its overall business strategy 
and future growth, it remains committed to expanding its IP 
portfolio and fostering innovation across all aspects of its 
business.
In FY 2025-26, the Company continued expanding IP including 
emerging technology domains such as digital and Artificial 
Intelligence (AI). The Company also filed 120 patents and achieved 
a landmark figure of 1,200+ cumulative filed patents. Building on 
the initiative launched in the previous year, the Company actively 
socialised its IP Handbook through training. Also, the IP Reward 
Policy continued to motivate and incentivise employees for their 
innovative contribution.
The Company undertakes periodic reviews of IP processes to 
strengthen IP management. It proactively identifies opportunities 
for protection across evolving technology areas, while 
maintaining strong internal controls and preventive measures to 
respect the IP rights of third parties. In recognition of various IP 
efforts, Maruti Suzuki was named among the 'Top 50 IP Driven 
Organisations' at the CII IP Awards, 2025.
Maruti Suzuki continuously monitors the evolving threat 
landscape and maintains a proactive stance toward incident 
management. No material cyber security incidents were reported 
during FY 2025–26, reflecting the effectiveness of the preventive 
and monitoring mechanisms in place. As security alerts increase, 
artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) tools have 
become key to effective security threat detection and response.
To strengthen organisational preparedness, Maruti Suzuki has 
institutionalised a structured cyber security awareness and 
training program for employees. This includes pre-onboarding 
and induction-level sensitisation, annual mandatory Information 
Security and Cybersecurity compliance training for all employees, 
and periodic targeted interventions. The Company also conducts 
phishing simulation exercises, followed by focused trainings for 
identified groups, along with regular dissemination of cyber 
security advisories through email campaigns.
A third-party risk management program for parts suppliers has 
been implemented in collaboration with the Supply Chain vertical 
to identify supplier risks and plan countermeasures to minimise 
the risk of business interruption due to an adverse cyber event 
at the supplier end.
The Company follows a philosophy of continuous improvement 
in cyber security capabilities, with ongoing investments in 
advanced technologies, process enhancements, and governance 
mechanisms to address emerging risks and ensure business 
continuity.

Financial Highlights
The total income was I 1,876,580 million as against I 1,579,326 
million in the previous year showing an increase of 18.82%. 
Sale of vehicles in the domestic market was 1,974,939 units 
as compared to 1,901,681 units in the previous year showing 
an increase of 3.85%. Total number of vehicles exported was 
447,774 units as compared to 332,585 units in the previous year 
showing an increase of 34.63%.
Profit before tax (PBT) was I 188,629 million against I 194,127 
million showing a decrease of 2.83% and Profit After Tax (PAT) 
stood at I 144,454 million against I 142,976 million in the previous 
year showing an increase of 1.03%.
Dividend
The Board recommends a dividend of I 140/- per equity share 
of I 5/- each for the year ended 31st March 2026 amounting to 
I 44,016 million. No amount was carried to General Reserve. 
The Company has formulated a dividend distribution policy and 
the same is available on the website of the Company at the 
web-link https://www.marutisuzuki.com/pdf-viewer?pdf=%2Fc

Brief outline on CSR policy of the company
	
The Company’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) 
initiatives are in the areas of Community Development, 
Skill Development and Road Safety. To create a visible 
and lasting impact, the Company focuses on a few CSR 
programmes rather than spreading resources thin over 
several projects.
	
Under the Community Development theme, the Company 
is committed to improving the well-being of the community 
by implementing social projects in designated villages 
around company’s facilities and local communities. To 
create a positive and meaningful impact on the lives of 
communities, the projects are undertaken to strengthen 
the common community infrastructure and improve health, 
education, water, and sanitation services, ensuring all-
round development. Standout examples include a multi-
specialty tertiary care hospital and a modern CBSE school 
in Gujarat, and holistic village development initiatives 
targeting ultra-local problems in the designated villages, 
significantly improving the lives of local residents. In 
recent years, the Company has expanded its focus to 
address critical social priorities such as anemia reduction, 
promotion of menstrual hygiene among school children, 
large‑scale tree plantation, establishment of STEM 
laboratories, and development of school libraries.
	
The Company supports the measures to popularise the 
usage of Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) produced 
by biogas plants across India among the farmers. The 
project is implemented in phases including research on 
FOM, extension work comprising on-field demonstration 
& farmers connect program. Fermented Organic Manure 
(FOM) aligns with multiple SDGs and offers multiple 
benefits, including improved soil health, reduction in usage 
of chemical fertilisers, curb stubble burning, reduce the 
greenhouse gas emission, generate rural employment 
opportunities across the value chain, etc. contributing to 
sustainable agricultural development.
	
Through Skill Development initiatives, the Company focuses 
on skill development and employability enhancement of 
youth, aligned with industry requirements. As part of these 
initiatives, the company improves the quality of training, 
develops and upgrades training infrastructure including 
residential hostel facilities, facilitates holistic learning of 
students, through industry aligned curriculum as well as 
add-on courses, training of the trainers, and provides 
study material, scholarships, and practical training. 
The Japan India Institute for Manufacturing (JIM), the 
company’s flagship skill development institute, is a key 
institute for vocational skill development that trains the 
youth in vocational courses through the latest technology 
tools, industry exposure through on-the-job training and 
shop-floor practices based on Japanese manufacturing 
methods. The JIMs serve as centres of excellence and 
model ITI, preparing industry‑ready workforce for the 
manufacturing ecosystem. In addition to long‑term 
courses, the Company has recently introduced short‑term 
training programs aimed at upskilling the existing workforce 
through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and enhancing 
employment opportunities for youth through the Recruit, 
Train and Deploy (RTD) model. 
	
Beyond JIMs, the company upgrades selected government 
ITIs for manufacturing trades and automotive service 
trades. Through these initiatives, advanced labs are being 
set up, and industry relevant training is being provided 
to ITI trainers and students, aiming to build a workforce 
ready for the manufacturing industry. Ultimately, these 
interventions aim to progressively bring government ITIs 
at par with JIMs in terms of training quality, infrastructure, 
and industry relevance.
	
In the area of Road Safety, the company is dedicated 
to implementing the 5E approach, which encompasses 
Education, Evaluation, Enforcement, Engineering, and 
Emergency care. One of the most significant projects in 
the road safety area is the large-scale rollout of Automated 
Driving Test Tracks (ADTTs). ADTTs completely automate 
the driver license testing process, eliminating human 
bias and ensuring only the drivers with requisite skills 
receive the license. Additionally, in collaboration with 
State Governments, the company manages the Institute 
of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTRs) and Road 
Safety Knowledge Centers (RSKCs) to equip drivers 
with the necessary knowledge and skills. To strengthen 
traffic law enforcement, the company also implements 
Integrated Traffic Safety Management System with real-
time monitoring and surveillance system to support law 
enforcement, surveillance and promote disciplined driving 
behaviour. To improve emergency care, the company also 
imparts first responder training to the commercial drivers 
and other stakeholders.
	
The Company encourages and recognises its employees 
for volunteering in the community by serving and sharing 
their expertise and skills to contribute to the local 
community development.
